newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds shed strong early gains to finish lower after the double whammy of strong U.S. new home sales data and a surprise rate hike by the Bank of England, dealers said.

Recent gains were founded on U.S. advances and the stronger-than-expected September new home sales of 816,000 units, the second highest level since April 1996, quickly soured the market there, one trader said.
"We had really quite a good feeling at the start, but as soon as the U.S. turned then we were digging down too in no time," he said.
The bank of England's decision to raise its base lending rate by 25 basis points to 6.00 percent also helped dissipate the market's earlier, cheery tone by briefly smacking Bunds, one dealer said.
Guilders slightly outperformed Bunds into the close, with the ten-year yield discount moving out to 13 basis points from 12 on Tuesday, and the 30-year edging out to 21 from 19.

The yield curve flattened further through the day with the 5-10 year spread narrowing appreciably to near 94 basis points from around 100 on Monday. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
